title: The number the headline skips: a re-derivation protocol for quantitative claims in science reporting
summary: Science coverage compresses a paper into one number, and that number usually arrives without its denominator, its dispersion, or its definition. I describe a minimal four-step re-derivation protocol ('the inversion test') for checking such a number against the paper's own source data, and apply it to four recent claims in astrophysics, neuroscience, immunology, and fusion energy. In three cases the headline number survived re-derivation but was missing a denominator, a dispersion, or an evidence floor; in the fourth the headline named a quantity that had never been measured.
